claims.text: The starting material is a titanium- and nickel-primary high-entropy alloy.
The intervention is the addition of 5 at.% Ti.
Adding 5 at.% Ti to the titanium- and nickel-primary alloy will induce precipitation.
The Ti-induced precipitate will be the (CoNi)3Ti phase.
Precipitation hardening will improve the alloy's elevated-temperature mechanical properties.
The Ti-modified alloy will have better elevated-temperature mechanical properties than the corresponding alloy without the Ti intervention.
Hardness, yield strength, and ductility are the mechanical-property responses used to evaluate the intervention.
The hypothesis is falsified if the Ti-added alloy shows no improvement in elevated-temperature mechanical properties relative to the control alloy.

contradictions.description: The starting and baseline materials are described as titanium-primary, yet Ti is also presented as the added intervention and the baseline as being 'without Ti addition.' It is unclear whether the control contains primary-level Ti and receives no incremental Ti, or contains no Ti.

The intervention says 5 at.% Ti is added, whereas the boundary can be read as specifying a final composition of 5 at.% Ti. These are not equivalent, and a final 5 at.% Ti content is difficult to reconcile with the description of Ti as a primary constituent without a complete composition.
